# Mobile Pet Oncology

We proudly serve pets in New Jersey and Pennsylvania.

Let’s find the right treatment option.

Every pet is different, and we work hard to create a customized treatment plan for your furry family member.

##### Chemotherapy

Our goal during pet cancer treatment services is to ensure the highest quality of life possible for every pet undergoing treatment. Chemotherapy in animals is given at palliative doses, compared to humans which receive curative intent dosing. This difference results in most pets tolerating chemotherapy well, adverse reactions are only reported by owners in 10%-15% of pets.

We encourage owners to share their concerns and observations with us at each visit prior to treatment. This feedback provides us with valuable information on how a patient is feeling during their chemotherapy regimen.

Click here to complete our Chemotherapy Consent Form.

## About Private Veterinary Specialties

Private Veterinary Specialties L.L.C provides on-site medical oncology services for veterinarians and their clients ​at five different locations around​ New Jersey. This unique approach allows ​some ​pet owners to stay with their primary veterinarian’s office while their pet receives cancer care instead of being referred to another facility. Our multiple locations around NJ are strategically placed so that we can cut down travel time for owners.

We provide veterinary cancer consultations, diagnostic procedures, mobile chemotherapy, and immunotherapy. Complete lab services include blood work, flow cytometry, cytology, and histology. Essentially, we bring the specialists to you.

What we do

## Medical Oncology Services

We seek to provide pet owners with the best possible veterinary care for their beloved furry family members. Our mobile department provides convenience by offering 5 locations, allowing owners to take advantage of our specialist cancer care without needing to travel far.

Image: Immunotherapy

#### Immunotherapy

Immunotherapy enhances the pet’s immune system to target cancer cells, using vaccines for a targeted and less toxic approach.

Image: Chemotherapy (2)

#### Chemotherapy

Chemotherapy in animals is given at palliative doses, compared to humans who receive curative intent dosing.

Image: Pain Management And Palliative Care

#### Pain Management & Palliative Care

Pain management & palliative care for pets improve their quality of life, alleviate suffering, and support pet owners.

## We’ll be with you every step of the way.

We provide on-site medical oncology services for veterinarians and pet owners ​at five convenient locations around central New Jersey. Contact our experienced team at Private Veterinary Specialties for expert pet oncology with compassionate veterinary care.

# About Private
Veterinary Specialties

## Who Are We

Private Veterinary Specialties L.L.C provides on-site medical oncology services at five different locations for veterinarians and their clients throughout central New Jersey. This unique approach allows some pet owners to stay with their primary veterinarian’s office while their pet receives cancer care or be seen at one of our convenient locations.

We provide veterinary cancer consultations, diagnostic procedures, mobile chemotherapy, and immunotherapy. Complete lab services include blood work, flow cytometry, cytology, and histology. Essentially, we bring the specialists to you.

## Our Experienced Team Can Help

The founder of PVS, Dr. Hamilton, has assembled a talented team of professionals for the practice. Private Veterinary Specialties specializes in pet oncology. However, our team has cared for dogs, cats, and various animal species, including those in zoo habitats.

Image: Dr. Hamilton

Image: dottes (1)

### Dr. Hamilton, DVM, DACVIM(O)

Veterinarian / Owner

Dr. Hamilton has worked in veterinary medicine his entire life, starting as kennel help at 14. After completing his undergraduate degree in psychology, he stayed at Colorado State University to complete his doctorate in veterinary medicine. Dr. Hamilton spent two years in general practice in Las Vegas, then went on to start his oncology residency at Michigan State University. As a board-certified veterinary oncologist, Dr. Hamilton has been commissioned to start multiple oncology departments in the northeast, participate in clinical trials, and is asked to lecture frequently.

Dr. Hamilton has provided mobile oncology care in NJ since 2011, seeing patients most commonly from Hunterdon, Somerset, Warren, and Union counties. Dr. H deeply enjoys bettering the lives of oncology patients and working with their owners to ensure the best quality of life possible. This passion motivated Dr. Hamilton to bring oncology specialty care to the general practice in 2017, allowing pet owners, veterinarians, and specialists to work together in one setting.

Dr. Angela Taylor graduated magna cum laude from University of Georgia's veterinary school. Following a small animal medicine and surgery internship at the Animal Medical Center in New York, she underwent oncology training at the Royal Veterinary College (UK) and received a Master's degree with merit and ACVIM diplomate credentials. She has been a faculty member with the RVC's Oncology service and worked in private practice in New York, and she now enjoys being a part of the Mount Laurel Animal Hospital team.

Dr. Taylor holds a certificate in higher education and is a fellow of the Higher Education Academy (HEA). She is a member of the AVMA, ACVIM (Oncology), NJVMA, and SJVMA. In conjunction with traditional therapeutics, she is also interested in novel options such as tyrosine kinase inhibitors and low-dose (metronomic) chemotherapy. # Oncology

## Michelle Morges, DVM, MS, DACVIM (Oncology), cVMA

Dr. Michelle Morges earned her bachelor’s degree at the University of Delaware. She graduated from Colorado State University’s Veterinary School in 2009.  Dr. Morges completed a residency in medical oncology at CSU in 2014, and while there, earned a concurrent Master’s degree.  Working for years in private specialty practice, Dr. Morges has developed a strong interest in patients with advanced/metastatic disease, geriatric cancer patients, and uses a multimodality approach in many of her cases. As a medical oncologist, Dr. Morges is available to provide or confirm a cancer diagnosis, provide detailed information regarding a cancer diagnosis in your pet, perform tumor staging tests, administer treatments such as chemotherapy and/or immunotherapy, recommend collaborative treatments such as surgery and/or radiation therapy, and provide palliative cancer care. Dr. Morges is also trained in medical acupuncture.

In her free time, Dr. Morges is an avid equestrian, enjoys yoga, traveling, and spending time with her 2 dogs, 3 cats, and her horse “Moxie”.

## Dr. Morges works in tandem with your pet’s primary care veterinarian to treat an array of cancers including:

  * Lymphoma
  * Hemangiosarcoma
  * Osteosarcoma
  * Mast cell tumors and other skin tumors
  * Tumors of the endocrine system
  * Tumors of the central nervous system
  * Many other types of cancer/neoplasia

A cancer diagnosis can be scary and treatment options confusing. Many patients diagnosed with cancer can lead happy, healthy lives while undergoing treatment. There are many options that can be considered depending upon the diagnosis and we are here to help!

If chemotherapy is elected as a treatment option, it is administered at Animal Emergency and Referral Associates on an appointment only basis. Each appointment will take each owner approximately thirty minutes from the time they walk in until the time they leave. Appointments are typically on an outpatient basis Monday through Friday. Drop off appointments are available at no extra charge if our appointment times do not meet the needs of the client. During each appointment we will ask a history of how the pet has been doing, perform a physical exam and then speak with each owner regarding their pet’s progress, answering any questions that they may have.

**Radiation Therapy**
Radiation therapy is a form of local therapy used to treat cancer and other diseases. Some cancers respond very well to radiation and can be cured. However, not all cancers are amenable to radiation. An oncologist will discuss this with the owner along with the prognosis and length of treatment as this varies for each type of cancer. Our oncologists will work in conjunction with veterinarians boarded in Veterinary Radiation Oncology, Medical Oncology and Internal Medicine to establish a plan that is appropriate for each pet’s disease.

If radiation therapy is elected as a treatment option, it is performed in Clifton at The Veterinary MRI and Radiotherapy Center of New Jersey. ## Our Services in New Jersey

Let’s find the right treatment option. Every pet is different, and we work hard to create
a customized treatment plan for your furry family member.

##### Chemotherapy

Our goal during pet cancer treatment services is to ensure the highest quality of life possible for every pet undergoing treatment. Chemotherapy in animals is given at palliative doses, compared to humans, which receive curative intent dosing. This difference results in most pets tolerating chemotherapy well; adverse reactions are only reported by owners in 10%-15% of pets.

We encourage owners to share their concerns and observations with us at each visit prior to treatment. This feedback provides valuable information on how a patient feels during their chemotherapy regimen.

Click here to complete our Chemotherapy Consent Form.

##### Immunotherapy

This therapy is currently available for melanoma. 
##### Consultation For Radiation Therapy

PVS does not perform radiation therapy. However, we counsel owners on which cancers will likely respond to radiation. We can also facilitate your pets’ appointments at radiation facilities in the area. After radiation is completed, we provide long-term support and cancer monitoring.

##### Pain Management And Palliative Care

Pain control is our top priority and a significant concern for most owners. During each visit, we work hard to address any pain concerns owners have or any pain noted in a patient. Pain control is essential to a good quality of life.

##### Genetic Tumor Testing

We now offer VetOmics tumor testing for dogs. This genetic test is provided to further evaluate pet tumors for genetic mutations, which we may be able to target with compounded human medications for personalized therapy. This testing is elected by owners who want advanced cancer care and those who are open to trying novel therapies with human medicines. For some pets, these human medications can target the mutation that may drive an individual cancer to grow and spread.

Mobile department

Private Veterinary Specialties LLC provides medical oncology services for veterinarians and their clients at multiple locations.
